  "text": "Every Thursday, someone left a lemon on the library steps.

At first, Nell assumed it had fallen from a shopping bag. She put it beside the returns desk, where it remained until the cleaner took it home. The following week, another appeared, bright against the rain-dark stone.

By November, the staff had theories. A secret admirer. A gardening club protest. An unusually modest harvest festival.

Nell began arriving early.

On the fourth Thursday, she caught an elderly man lowering a lemon from his coat pocket. He placed it carefully beside the handrail.

“Could I ask what that’s for?” she said.

He straightened. “Overdue fees.”

“We stopped charging those three years ago.”

“I know. Your predecessor told me.”

He looked through the glass doors toward the children’s corner.

“In 1968, I borrowed a book about growing citrus. Kept it forty-one years. When I finally brought it back, the librarian asked whether I’d had any luck.”

“And had you?”

“One tree. Took a while.”

Nell waited.

“She said I could pay her in lemons.”

The previous librarian had died in August. Nell still found her handwriting on scraps tucked inside reference books: useful telephone numbers, corrected dates, reminders to order glue.

“She never mentioned it,” Nell said.

The man rubbed his thumb over a leaf still attached to the stem.

“I can stop.”

“No,” Nell said. “Thursday’s good.”

She unlocked the doors and found a shallow bowl in the staff kitchen. Then she set it on the returns desk, with the lemon in the middle.

Next Thursday, she would ask his name."
